video_title: Why CQRS Exists: One Model Can't Optimize for Writes and Reads
core_insight: CQRS separates the model for changing state from the model for reading state because writes need integrity and reads need speed and shape, and one model cannot optimize for both.

scenes.voice: Why does a simple CRUD app start to hurt as it grows? The same model ends up doing two jobs.
scenes.visual: Split screen: left shows write form with validation, right shows dashboard with charts. Same database icon in middle with contention arrows.

scenes.voice: Writes need integrity. They enforce business rules, authorization, transactions. Reads need speed and shape. Low latency, denormalized views for specific UIs.
scenes.visual: Two requirement cards appear: Writes = integrity, invariants, transactions. Reads = speed, shape, denormalized.

scenes.voice: With classic CRUD, the same tables serve both. Read queries contend with writes. New views mean joins or changing the write model. Scaling reads forces scaling writes too.
scenes.visual: Single service box with Command and Query arrows hitting same DB. Red contention icons, growing query complexity.

scenes.voice: Reasonable first fix is read replicas or materialized views. That helps reads, but the write model still shapes the data and business logic leaks into queries.
scenes.visual: Read replica added, but schema still normalized. Query still doing joins to shape response.

scenes.voice: CQRS says separate intent to change state from intent to observe state. Commands change state with validation. Queries are read-only, optimized projections.
scenes.visual: Bank teller window vs lobby display board analogy. Teller processes deposit, board shows balances.

scenes.voice: Write side handles commands, persists to a normalized write model, emits events. Projector builds denormalized read models for each use case. Queries hit those read models.
scenes.visual: Flow diagram animates step by step.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  Client -->|Command| CH[Command Handler]
  CH --> WM[(Write Model)]
  WM -->|Domain Event| Bus
  Bus --> RH[Read Model Projector]
  RH --> RM[(Read Model)]
  Client -->|Query| QH[Query Handler]
  QH --> RM

scenes.voice: You gain independent scaling and clean domain logic. You pay eventual consistency and more operational complexity. Two schemas, projection failures, idempotency.
scenes.visual: Scale icons up on read side only. Warning icons for lag, projection, complexity.

scenes.voice: Use CQRS when read and write workloads, SLAs, or team boundaries diverge. Avoid it when a single model is still enough.
scenes.visual: Decision diamond: divergent scale / query complexity / ownership? Yes → CQRS. No → single model.
scenes.on_screen_text: Split only when divergence justifies cost

mental_model: Think of a bank teller window for changes with strict rules, and a lobby display board for observations optimized for viewing. When the needs of changing and viewing diverge, give them separate models connected by projections.
final_takeaway: CQRS separates writes for integrity from reads for speed and shape. Value is independent scaling and clean domain logic; cost is eventual consistency and complexity.
